neutral_facts.value: The accused, who were the son and associates of the deceased, were implicated in the death of the deceased, who was found dead by his brother. The prosecution alleged that the accused had a property dispute with the deceased and that the accused fled the scene. The accused were apprehended, and items such as a rusted iron rod and a sweater were recovered. The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence, including witness testimonies about the accused's presence at the scene and Call Detail Records (CDRs) to establish their location. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the IPC and sentenced them to life imprisonment. The High Court upheld the conviction, but the Supreme Court quashed the conviction, finding that the prosecution failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.

quotes.text: The appeals challenge the judgment and order dated 5th August 2014 passed by the High Court of Delhi at New Delhi in Criminal Appeal Nos. 1242, 936 and 1136 of 2013, thereby aﬃrming the judgment and order dated 17th May 2013 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge-II (North-West), Rohini Courts, Delhi.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused Prem Singh fled the scene of the incident and was apprehended two days later. They relied on the testimony of Jai Singh and Naresh Kumar, as well as the Call Detail Records (CDRs) to establish the guilt of the accused. The prosecution also claimed that the accused had a history of conflict with the deceased and that they committed the murder.

quotes.text: The prosecution story, shorn of details, is as under: 3.1 On 10th September 2009 at around 04.15 pm, complainant-Surat Singh, brother of the deceased Hoshiyar Singh, came to the house of the deceased and found him lying dead on the cot. In the meantime, his elder brother Jai Singh (PW-20) also reached the spot. The deceased was taken to the hospital where he was declared dead.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to establish the case beyond reasonable doubt. They emphasized the unreliability of the circumstantial evidence, particularly the last seen theory and the CDRs. The defence also highlighted the flaws in the identification process and the lack of conclusive evidence linking the accused to the crime.

quotes.text: The prosecution has utterly failed to prove the case as they need to prove the incriminating circumstances beyond reasonable doubt. The evidence with regard to last seen theory is totally unreliable. The evidence regarding the CDRs also is one which does not inspire any conﬁdence.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that for a conviction based on circumstantial evidence, the circumstances from which the conclusion of guilt is drawn must be fully established, consistent only with the hypothesis of the accused's guilt, and exclude every possible hypothesis except that the accused is guilty. The court emphasized that suspicion cannot replace proof beyond reasonable doubt.

quotes.text: It is a settled principle of law that however strong a suspicion may be, it cannot take place of a proof beyond reasonable doubt. In the light of these guiding principles, we will have to consider the present case.
